proposals.before: The National History Institute now holds Chen Daren's Jin-dynasty "Liao Ritual Treatise," which records their native customs, and also a "Miscellaneous Liao Rites," largely in the Chinese style.
proposals.after: The National History Institute now holds Jin Chen Daren's "Liao Ritual Treatise," which records their native customs, and also a "Miscellaneous Liao Rites," largely in the Chinese style.
proposals.reason: Chinese 金陳大任 marks Jin-dynasty affiliation before the name; idiomatic 'Chen Daren's Jin-dynasty' reverses that attribution.

proposals.before: Whoever hit the willow pledged goods against the marker of the willow's crown and robes; whoever missed pledged crown and robes as stake.
proposals.after: Whoever hit the willow took as pledge the crown and robes of the willow's marker; whoever missed pledged his own crown and robes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 中柳者質誌柳者冠服 means hitters take the marker's pledged regalia; the literal reverses the pledge direction.

decisions.after: The National History Institute now holds a "Liao Ritual Treatise" by Chen Daren of the Jin dynasty, which records Liao native customs, and also a "Miscellaneous Liao Rites," largely in the Chinese style.
decisions.reason: 金 identifies Chen Daren as a Jin-dynasty author. The revised wording preserves that relationship in natural English instead of the awkward possessive ‘Jin Chen Daren's.’
中柳者質誌柳者冠服 means the hitter takes the willow-marker's crown and robes as pledge; the original literal reverses that direction, and the proposed wording matches 不中者以冠服質之 for the misser's own stake.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 中柳者質誌柳者冠服，不中者以冠服質之
